    AV_CHAN_BINAURAL_LEFT = 61,
    AV_CHAN_BINAURAL_RIGHT,

    /** Channel is empty can be safely skipped. */
    AV_CHAN_UNUSED = 0x200,

    /** Channel contains data, but its position is unknown. */
    AV_CHAN_UNKNOWN = 0x300,

    /**
     * Range of channels between AV_CHAN_AMBISONIC_BASE and
     * AV_CHAN_AMBISONIC_END represent Ambisonic components using the ACN system.
     *
     * Given a channel id `<i>` between AV_CHAN_AMBISONIC_BASE and
     * AV_CHAN_AMBISONIC_END (inclusive), the ACN index of the channel `<n>` is
     * `<n> = <i> - AV_CHAN_AMBISONIC_BASE`.
     *
     * @note these values are only used for AV_CHANNEL_ORDER_CUSTOM channel
     * orderings, the AV_CHANNEL_ORDER_AMBISONIC ordering orders the channels
     * implicitly by their position in the stream.
     */
    AV_CHAN_AMBISONIC_BASE = 0x400,
    // leave space for 1024 ids, which correspond to maximum order-32 harmonics,
    // which should be enough for the foreseeable use cases
    AV_CHAN_AMBISONIC_END  = 0x7ff,
};
objects.description: Enumerates all individual audio channel designations supported by FFmpeg, including native channel positions, special stereo downmix channels, binaural channels, and a reserved range for Ambisonic ACN components. Values are used to build masks, maps, and to query/describe channels.

objects.definition:
enum AVChannelOrder {
    /**
     * Only the channel count is specified, without any further information
     * about the channel order.
     */
    AV_CHANNEL_ORDER_UNSPEC,
    /**
     * The native channel order, i.e. the channels are in the same order in
     * which they are defined in the AVChannel enum. This supports up to 63
     * different channels.
     */
    AV_CHANNEL_ORDER_NATIVE,
    /**
     * The channel order does not correspond to any other predefined order and
     * is stored as an explicit map. For example, this could be used to support
     * layouts with 64 or more channels, or with empty/skipped (AV_CHAN_UNUSED)
     * channels at arbitrary positions.
     */
    AV_CHANNEL_ORDER_CUSTOM,
    /**
     * The audio is represented as the decomposition of the sound field into
     * spherical harmonics. Each channel corresponds to a single expansion
     * component. Channels are ordered according to ACN (Ambisonic Channel
     * Number).
     *
     * The channel with the index n in the stream contains the spherical
     * harmonic of degree l and order m given by
     * @code{.unparsed}
     *   l   = floor(sqrt(n)),
     *   m   = n - l * (l + 1).
     * @endcode
     *
     * Conversely given a spherical harmonic of degree l and order m, the
     * corresponding channel index n is given by
     * @code{.unparsed}
     *   n = l * (l + 1) + m.
     * @endcode
     *
     * Normalization is assumed to be SN3D (Schmidt Semi-Normalization)
     * as defined in AmbiX format $ 2.1.
     */
    AV_CHANNEL_ORDER_AMBISONIC,
    /**
     * Number of channel orders, not part of ABI/API
     */
    FF_CHANNEL_ORDER_NB
};
objects.description: Specifies how channels are ordered/represented in an AVChannelLayout: unspecified, native (enum order), custom explicit map, or Ambisonic (ACN). Used to interpret the union in AVChannelLayout.

Describes an audio channel layout: order scheme, channel count, and either a bitmask (native/ambisonic extras) or an explicit per-channel map (custom). Size is public ABI. Must be uninitialized with av_channel_layout_uninit; copy via av_channel_layout_copy when needed. Construction helpers provided in this header.

functions.name: avutil_version
functions.signature: unsigned avutil_version(void);
functions.description: Returns the LIBAVUTIL_VERSION_INT constant for the linked libavutil. Intended for runtime version checks or diagnostics.

functions.name: av_version_info
functions.signature: const char *av_version_info(void);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable, informative version string for the linked libavutil (e.g., release number or git describe). The format is not fixed and may change; it is for display only, not parsing.
requirements: Do not parse or depend on any particular format of the returned string.
The returned pointer remains valid for the lifetime of the process or library; do not free it.

functions.name: avutil_configuration
functions.signature: const char *avutil_configuration(void);
functions.description: Returns a string describing the build-time configuration options of the linked libavutil.
requirements: The returned pointer is owned by the library; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: avutil_license
functions.signature: const char *avutil_license(void);
functions.description: Returns a string containing the libavutil license text.
requirements: The returned pointer is owned by the library; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: av_get_media_type_string
functions.signature: const char *av_get_media_type_string(enum AVMediaType media_type);
functions.description: Returns a string describing the given AVMediaType, or NULL if the media_type is unknown.
requirements: Pass a valid AVMediaType enum value; handle a NULL return for unknown or unsupported values.
Do not modify or free the returned string.

functions.name: av_get_picture_type_char
functions.signature: char av_get_picture_type_char(enum AVPictureType pict_type);
functions.description: Returns a single character representing the given AVPictureType (e.g., 'I', 'P', 'B'); returns '?' if pict_type is unknown.
requirements: Pass a valid AVPictureType enum value; callers should handle the '?' result for unknown values.

functions.name: av_int_list_length_for_size
functions.signature: unsigned av_int_list_length_for_size(unsigned elsize, const void *list, uint64_t term);
functions.description: Computes the number of elements in an integer list of fixed-width elements, not counting the terminating element. Deprecated (guarded by FF_API_OPT_INT_LIST) and may not be available in future builds.
requirements: elsize must be one of: 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes.
list must be a non-NULL pointer to a contiguous array of integers with elements of size elsize.
The list must be terminated by a value equal to term, and memory must be readable up to and including the terminator.
term must be representable in the element type defined by elsize.
Behavior is undefined if the list is not properly terminated or if elsize is not one of the allowed sizes.

functions.name: av_get_time_base_q
functions.signature: AVRational av_get_time_base_q(void);
functions.description: Returns the fractional representation of the internal time base (typically { num=1, den=AV_TIME_BASE }). Useful for timestamp conversions.

functions.name: av_fourcc_make_string
functions.signature: char *av_fourcc_make_string(char *buf, uint32_t fourcc);
functions.description: Writes a textual representation of a FourCC (four-character code) into buf and returns buf.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least AV_FOURCC_MAX_STRING_SIZE bytes.
buf must be non-NULL and valid for writing.
fourcc may be any 32-bit value; callers should ensure desired endianness/encoding as appropriate.

functions.name: av_log
functions.signature: void av_log(void *avcl, int level, const char *fmt, ...) av_printf_format(3, 4);
functions.description: Logs a formatted message if level is <= current global log level. By default, messages go to stderr via the current logging callback (which can be replaced). Pass avcl as NULL for general logs or as a pointer to a struct whose first member is AVClass* for contextual logs. Use printf-style formatting in fmt and variadic args.
requirements: avcl may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to a struct whose first field is an AVClass*
level should use lavu_log_constants (e.g., AV_LOG_ERROR) and may include AV_LOG_C(x) for color
fmt must be a valid printf-compatible format string for the supplied arguments
Caller must provide arguments matching fmt to avoid undefined behavior

functions.name: av_log_once
functions.signature: void av_log_once(void* avcl, int initial_level, int subsequent_level, int *state, const char *fmt, ...) av_printf_format(5, 6);
functions.description: Logs a message once at initial_level, and on subsequent calls (with the same state) at subsequent_level. Uses the same callback mechanism as av_log. Useful for demoting repeated messages after the first occurrence.
requirements: state must point to a variable initialized to 0 before first use
The same state must not be accessed by two threads simultaneously
avcl may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to a struct whose first field is an AVClass*
initial_level and subsequent_level should use lavu_log_constants
fmt must be a valid printf-compatible format string for the supplied arguments
Caller must provide arguments matching fmt to avoid undefined behavior

functions.name: av_vlog
functions.signature: void av_vlog(void *avcl, int level, const char *fmt, va_list vl);
functions.description: Logs a formatted message using a pre-built va_list. Equivalent to av_log but takes a va_list instead of variadic arguments.
requirements: avcl must point to a struct whose first field is an AVClass* (documentation does not state NULL is allowed)
level should use lavu_log_constants (e.g., AV_LOG_ERROR)
fmt must be a valid printf-compatible format string
vl must be a valid va_list corresponding to fmt and initialized by the caller (e.g., via va_start)

functions.name: av_log_get_level
functions.signature: int av_log_get_level(void);
functions.description: Returns the current global logging level controlling which messages are emitted.

functions.name: av_log_set_level
functions.signature: void av_log_set_level(int level);
functions.description: Sets the current global logging level controlling which messages are emitted.
requirements: level should be one of the lavu_log_constants (e.g., AV_LOG_INFO) or a compatible value within the defined range

functions.name: av_log_set_callback
functions.signature: void av_log_set_callback(void (*callback)(void*, int, const char*, va_list));
functions.description: Installs a custom logging callback to replace the default logger. The callback receives the same parameters as the default logger and will be called for all log messages.
requirements: callback must be thread safe (may be called from multiple threads)
callback must match the exact signature (void*, int, const char*, va_list)
callback function pointer must remain valid while installed

functions.name: av_log_default_callback
functions.signature: void av_log_default_callback(void *avcl, int level, const char *fmt, va_list vl);
functions.description: The default logging callback used by FFmpeg. It prints messages to stderr and may colorize output. You can call it directly or let FFmpeg call it via the installed callback.
requirements: avcl must point to a struct whose first field is an AVClass*
level should use lavu_log_constants
fmt must be a valid printf-compatible format string
vl must be a valid va_list corresponding to fmt

functions.name: av_default_item_name
functions.signature: const char* av_default_item_name(void* ctx);
functions.description: Returns the default name for an AVClass-enabled context, typically the AVClass.class_name of the object pointed to by ctx.
requirements: ctx must be an AVClass context (i.e., a pointer to an object whose first field is an AVClass*)

functions.name: av_default_get_category
functions.signature: AVClassCategory av_default_get_category(void *ptr);
functions.description: Returns the category for an AVClass-enabled object. Details are not documented here; typically this uses the AVClass category or its get_category callback if provided.
requirements: ptr should be an AVClass-enabled object (first field AVClass*)

functions.name: av_log_format_line
functions.signature: void av_log_format_line(void *ptr, int level, const char *fmt, va_list vl, char *line, int line_size, int *print_prefix);
functions.description: Formats a single log line the same way as the default logging callback would, writing into the provided buffer and updating whether a prefix should be printed next time.
requirements: ptr should be an AVClass-enabled object (first field AVClass*) or NULL if allowed by caller usage
level should use lavu_log_constants
fmt must be a valid printf-compatible format string
vl must be a valid va_list corresponding to fmt
line must be a non-NULL buffer
line_size must be the size of line in bytes and > 0
print_prefix must point to a persistent int initially set to 1

functions.name: av_log_format_line2
functions.signature: int av_log_format_line2(void *ptr, int level, const char *fmt, va_list vl, char *line, int line_size, int *print_prefix);
functions.description: Formats a single log line like the default callback and returns the number of characters that would have been written (excluding the null terminator). Supports truncation reporting and optional NULL buffer when line_size is 0.
requirements: ptr should be an AVClass-enabled object (first field AVClass*) or NULL if allowed by caller usage
level should use lavu_log_constants
fmt must be a valid printf-compatible format string
vl must be a valid va_list corresponding to fmt
line may be NULL only if line_size is 0; otherwise must be a valid buffer
line_size must be the size of line in bytes; at most line_size-1 chars are written plus a null terminator
print_prefix must point to a persistent int initially set to 1
Caller should check the return value: negative on error; if >= line_size, output was truncated

functions.name: av_log_set_flags
functions.signature: void av_log_set_flags(int arg);
functions.description: Sets logging behavior flags that affect how messages are printed (e.g., skipping repeats, including level, time, or date/time).
requirements: arg is a bitmask of AV_LOG_* flags such as AV_LOG_SKIP_REPEATED, AV_LOG_PRINT_LEVEL, AV_LOG_PRINT_TIME, AV_LOG_PRINT_DATETIME

functions.name: av_log_get_flags
functions.signature: int av_log_get_flags(void);
functions.description: Returns the current logging behavior flags bitmask.

functions.name: av_strerror
functions.signature: int av_strerror(int errnum, char *errbuf, size_t errbuf_size);
functions.description: Formats a human-readable description of an AVERROR code into the provided buffer. Intended for converting negative libav* error codes (e.g., values from AVERROR(...)) into strings for logging or display. On failure, sets errno and still writes a generic message describing the provided error code into errbuf.
requirements: errnum should be an AVERROR-style error code (typically negative, possibly produced via AVERROR(...)).
errbuf must be a valid, writable pointer to a memory buffer.
errbuf_size specifies the size in bytes of errbuf and must accurately reflect the buffer length; if too small, the message may be truncated.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; a negative value indicates that a specific description was not found (errno is set), though a generic message is still written.

functions.name: av_make_error_string
functions.signature: static inline char *av_make_error_string(char *errbuf, size_t errbuf_size, int errnum);
functions.description: Convenience inline wrapper around av_strerror that fills the provided buffer with a textual description of the given AVERROR code and returns the same buffer pointer. Useful for immediate, inline formatting (also used by the av_err2str macro).
requirements: errbuf must be a valid, writable pointer to a memory buffer that remains valid for any subsequent use of the returned pointer.
errbuf_size specifies the size in bytes of errbuf and must accurately reflect the buffer length; if too small, the message may be truncated.
errnum should be an AVERROR-style error code (typically negative).
Callers should not assume success solely from the return value (which is errbuf); if needed, call av_strerror directly and check its return value for detailed error handling.
When used via av_err2str, the temporary buffer provided by the macro has size AV_ERROR_MAX_STRING_SIZE and the resulting pointer must only be used as a function argument (not stored).

functions.name: av_malloc
functions.signature: void *av_malloc(size_t size);
functions.description: Allocates a memory block of the requested size with alignment suitable for all memory accesses (including vectorized operations on supported CPUs). Returns NULL on allocation failure. Intended as the primary allocator for libavutil/FFmpeg code paths requiring aligned heap memory.
requirements: size is the number of bytes to allocate
Allocation is subject to a built-in per-allocation upper limit (default INT_MAX) which can be changed via av_max_alloc()
Returned pointer must be freed with av_free() or av_freep()
On success, memory contents are uninitialized

functions.name: av_mallocz
functions.signature: void *av_mallocz(size_t size);
functions.description: Allocates an aligned memory block and sets all bytes in the block to zero. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: size is the number of bytes to allocate and zero
Allocation is subject to the current per-allocation maximum (default INT_MAX, configurable via av_max_alloc())
Returned pointer must be freed with av_free() or av_freep()

functions.name: av_malloc_array
functions.signature: void *av_malloc_array(size_t nmemb, size_t size);
functions.description: Allocates an aligned memory block for an array of nmemb elements, each of size bytes, without zeroing the contents.
requirements: Computes total size as nmemb * size; beware potential overflow (library may check, but callers should supply sensible values)
Allocation is subject to the per-allocation maximum (default INT_MAX)
Returned pointer must be freed with av_free() or av_freep()

functions.name: av_calloc
functions.signature: void *av_calloc(size_t nmemb, size_t size);
functions.description: Allocates an aligned zero-initialized memory block for an array of nmemb elements, each of size bytes.
requirements: Computes total size as nmemb * size; callers should ensure values are sensible
Allocation is subject to the per-allocation maximum (default INT_MAX)
Returned pointer must be freed with av_free() or av_freep()

functions.name: av_realloc
functions.signature: void *av_realloc(void *ptr, size_t size);
functions.description: Allocates, reallocates, or frees a memory block. If ptr is NULL and size > 0, allocates a new block. Otherwise resizes the existing block to size bytes. Returns a pointer to the resized block, or NULL on failure. Unlike av_malloc(), returned pointers are not guaranteed to be aligned.
requirements: ptr must be either NULL or a pointer previously returned by av_realloc() (or compatible av_malloc/av_realloc family)
If size is zero, a pointer may still be returned and must be freed; do not assume NULL
Returned pointer (when non-NULL) must be freed with av_free()/av_freep()
Alignment is not guaranteed; do not rely on vector-friendly alignment

functions.name: av_reallocp
functions.signature: int av_reallocp(void *ptr, size_t size);
functions.description: Like av_realloc() but operates through a pointer-to-pointer. If *ptr is NULL and size > 0 it allocates; if size is zero it frees *ptr; otherwise it resizes. On success updates *ptr and returns 0; on failure returns a negative AVERROR code and frees the original block to avoid leaks. Alignment is not guaranteed.
requirements: ptr must point to a pointer variable that is either NULL or was allocated by the av_malloc/av_realloc family
If size is zero, the memory pointed to by *ptr is freed
On failure, the original memory is freed and *ptr is set accordingly; caller must handle the negative return code
Alignment of the newly allocated memory is not guaranteed

functions.name: av_realloc_f
functions.signature: void *av_realloc_f(void *ptr, size_t nelem, size_t elsize);
functions.description: Reallocates a block for an array, allocating nelem * elsize bytes after checking for multiplication overflow. On failure it frees the input block to avoid leaks (unlike plain realloc patterns). On success returns the resized block pointer. Also used to allocate when ptr is NULL and nelem > 0.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or previously allocated by the av_malloc/av_realloc family
The product nelem * elsize is overflow-checked; if overflow or allocation failure occurs, the input block is freed and NULL is returned
Returned pointer must be freed with av_free()/av_freep()
Alignment is not guaranteed (same caveats as av_realloc())

functions.name: av_realloc_array
functions.signature: void *av_realloc_array(void *ptr, size_t nmemb, size_t size);
functions.description: Allocates/reallocates/frees an array block to hold nmemb elements of given size after checking for multiplication overflow. Returns a pointer to the resized block or NULL on failure. Alignment is not guaranteed.
requirements: ptr must be NULL or previously allocated by the av_malloc/av_realloc family
The product nmemb * size is overflow-checked
If nmemb is zero, the returned pointer (if any) must still be freed; do not assume NULL
Returned pointer must be freed with av_free()/av_freep()
Alignment is not guaranteed

functions.name: av_reallocp_array
functions.signature: int av_reallocp_array(void *ptr, size_t nmemb, size_t size);
functions.description: Pointer-to-pointer variant to allocate or resize an array of nmemb elements of given size with overflow checking. Returns 0 on success or a negative AVERROR code on failure. On failure, the original memory is freed. Alignment is not guaranteed.
requirements: ptr must point to a pointer variable that is NULL or was allocated by the av_malloc/av_realloc family
The product nmemb * size is overflow-checked
If nmemb is zero, any allocated memory must still be freed by the caller when no longer needed
On failure, the original buffer is freed and the pointer is set accordingly; caller must handle negative return code
Alignment is not guaranteed

functions.name: av_fast_realloc
functions.signature: void *av_fast_realloc(void *ptr, unsigned int *size, size_t min_size);
functions.description: Ensures a buffer is at least min_size bytes. If ptr is NULL, allocates a new uninitialized buffer. If the existing buffer is too small, reallocates it and updates *size. On failure returns NULL and sets *size to 0; the original buffer (ptr) is left unchanged and not freed.
requirements: ptr may be NULL or a previously allocated buffer
size must be a valid pointer to the current capacity (in bytes) of ptr; it will be updated on success or set to 0 on failure
min_size is the required minimal size in bytes
On NULL return, the original buffer is unchanged; caller is responsible for freeing it if aborting
Returned non-NULL pointer must be freed with av_free()/av_freep() when no longer needed

functions.name: av_fast_malloc
functions.signature: void av_fast_malloc(void *ptr, unsigned int *size, size_t min_size);
functions.description: Ensures a buffer is at least min_size bytes, possibly reusing the existing one. Unlike av_fast_realloc(), current contents may not be preserved and on error the old buffer is freed and *ptr set to NULL; no special leak handling is required.
requirements: ptr must point to a pointer variable to a buffer; *ptr may be NULL
size must point to the current capacity (in bytes); it will be updated to the new allocated size or set to 0 on failure
min_size is the required minimal size in bytes
On failure, the old buffer is freed and *ptr becomes NULL; do not attempt to free it again
Any newly allocated space is uninitialized

functions.name: av_fast_mallocz
functions.signature: void av_fast_mallocz(void *ptr, unsigned int *size, size_t min_size);
functions.description: Like av_fast_malloc() but any newly allocated space is zero-initialized. Reused (pre-existing) buffer contents are not cleared. On error the old buffer is freed and *ptr set to NULL.
requirements: ptr must point to a pointer variable to a buffer; *ptr may be NULL
size must point to the current capacity (in bytes); it will be updated to the new allocated size or set to 0 on failure
min_size is the required minimal size in bytes
On failure, the old buffer is freed and *ptr becomes NULL; do not attempt to free it again

functions.name: av_free
functions.signature: void av_free(void *ptr);
functions.description: Frees a memory block previously allocated by av_malloc()/av_realloc() family functions. Accepts NULL (no action).
requirements: ptr must be a pointer obtained from the av_malloc/av_realloc family or NULL
Safe to pass NULL

functions.name: av_freep
functions.signature: void av_freep(void *ptr);
functions.description: Frees a memory block previously allocated by av_malloc()/av_realloc() family and sets the caller’s pointer to NULL to avoid dangling references. Accepts *ptr == NULL (no action).
requirements: ptr must point to a pointer variable allocated by the av_malloc/av_realloc family or to NULL
After return, *ptr is set to NULL
Do not pass a non-pointer or invalid address

functions.name: av_strdup
functions.signature: char *av_strdup(const char *s);
functions.description: Duplicates a NUL-terminated string using av_malloc()-family allocation and returns a newly allocated copy. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer
Returned string must be freed with av_free()/av_freep()

functions.name: av_strndup
functions.signature: char *av_strndup(const char *s, size_t len);
functions.description: Duplicates up to len bytes from the input string (not including the terminating byte) and returns a newly allocated NUL-terminated string. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: s must be a valid string pointer
len is the maximum number of bytes to copy (excluding terminator)
Returned string must be freed with av_free()/av_freep()

functions.name: av_memdup
functions.signature: void *av_memdup(const void *p, size_t size);
functions.description: Duplicates a memory buffer of size bytes using av_malloc()-family allocation and returns a newly allocated copy. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: p must point to a buffer of at least size bytes
size is the number of bytes to copy
Returned buffer must be freed with av_free()/av_freep()

functions.name: av_memcpy_backptr
functions.signature: void av_memcpy_backptr(uint8_t *dst, int back, int cnt);
functions.description: Copies cnt bytes into dst from a location back bytes before dst, supporting overlapping regions. If cnt > back, it creates a repeating pattern with period back. Useful for LZ-style back-references.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold cnt bytes
back must be > 0
cnt must be >= 0
The source region starting at dst - back must be valid for at least cnt bytes as the operation progresses

functions.name: av_dynarray_add
functions.signature: void av_dynarray_add(void *tab_ptr, int *nb_ptr, void *elem);
functions.description: Appends a pointer element to a dynamically growing array of pointers. Reallocates the array when its size reaches powers of two. On success updates the array pointer and increments *nb_ptr. On failure frees the array, sets *tab_ptr to NULL and *nb_ptr to 0.
requirements: tab_ptr must point to a variable holding the array pointer (i.e., pass &array where array is a pointer-to-element)
nb_ptr must be a valid pointer to the current number of elements
elem must be a pointer to an already allocated element to store
On failure, the array is freed and state reset; caller must not free the old array afterwards

functions.name: av_dynarray_add_nofree
functions.signature: int av_dynarray_add_nofree(void *tab_ptr, int *nb_ptr, void *elem);
functions.description: Appends a pointer element to a dynamically growing array of pointers without freeing on failure. Same semantics as av_dynarray_add(), but on failure it returns a negative error code and leaves the existing array untouched.
requirements: tab_ptr must point to a variable holding the array pointer
nb_ptr must be a valid pointer to the current number of elements
elem must be a pointer to an already allocated element
Returns >= 0 on success, negative AVERROR code otherwise; on failure the caller retains ownership of the existing array

functions.name: av_dynarray2_add
functions.signature: void *av_dynarray2_add(void **tab_ptr, int *nb_ptr, size_t elem_size, const uint8_t *elem_data);
functions.description: Appends a value element of elem_size bytes to a dynamically growing array of values. Reallocates when needed. On success updates the array pointer, increments *nb_ptr, and returns a pointer to the newly added element’s storage (optionally pre-filled from elem_data). On failure frees the array, sets *tab_ptr to NULL and *nb_ptr to 0.
requirements: tab_ptr must be a pointer to the array pointer (e.g., (void **)&array)
nb_ptr must be a valid pointer to the current element count
elem_size is the size in bytes of each element and should be > 0
elem_data may be NULL to leave the new element uninitialized; otherwise it must point to at least elem_size bytes to copy
On failure, the array is freed and state reset; caller must not free the old array afterwards

functions.name: av_size_mult
functions.signature: int av_size_mult(size_t a, size_t b, size_t *r);
functions.description: Multiplies two size_t values with overflow checking. Writes the product to *r on success. Returns 0 on success or AVERROR(EINVAL) if overflow occurs.
requirements: r must be a valid pointer to receive the result
a and b are treated as size_t multiplicands
Caller must check the return value for overflow indication

functions.name: av_max_alloc
functions.signature: void av_max_alloc(size_t max);
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of bytes that may be allocated in a single block by libavutil heap management functions. Default is INT_MAX. Affects all subsequent allocations in the process using libavutil.
requirements: Use with extreme caution; understand consequences before changing the limit
max is the new per-allocation limit in bytes and applies process-wide for libavutil allocations

functions.name: av_opt_set_defaults
functions.signature: void av_opt_set_defaults(void *s);
functions.description: Initialize all AVOption fields in an AVOptions-enabled struct to their default values. Use on objects whose first member is a pointer to an AVClass.
requirements: s must point to an AVOptions-enabled struct whose first member is a pointer to an AVClass.
The struct’s AVClass.option must reference a NULL-terminated AVOption array.

functions.name: av_opt_set_defaults2
functions.signature: void av_opt_set_defaults2(void *s, int mask, int flags);
functions.description: Initialize AVOption fields in s to defaults, but only those for which (opt->flags & mask) == flags.
requirements: s must point to an AVOptions-enabled struct (first member AVClass*).
mask and flags are combinations of AV_OPT_FLAG_* and control which options receive defaults.

functions.name: av_opt_free
functions.signature: void av_opt_free(void *obj);
functions.description: Free all allocated option-backed objects (e.g., strings, binaries, dicts) within an AVOptions-enabled object.
requirements: obj must be an AVOptions-enabled struct (first member AVClass*).
Caller remains responsible for freeing obj itself (this only frees option-allocated memory).

functions.name: av_opt_next
functions.signature: const AVOption *av_opt_next(const void *obj, const AVOption *prev);
functions.description: Iterate over AVOptions defined for an object or its AVClass. Pass NULL as prev to get the first, and the previous returned pointer to get the next. Returns NULL when finished.
requirements: obj must be an AVOptions-enabled struct or a double pointer to an AVClass describing it.
prev must be either NULL or a value previously returned by av_opt_next() for this obj.

functions.name: av_opt_child_next
functions.signature: void *av_opt_child_next(void *obj, void *prev);
functions.description: Iterate over actual AVOptions-enabled child objects of obj. Returns the next child or NULL when done.
requirements: obj must be an AVOptions-enabled parent supporting child iteration via AVClass.child_next.
prev must be NULL for the first call, then the last returned child pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_child_class_iterate
functions.signature: const AVClass *av_opt_child_class_iterate(const AVClass *parent, void **iter);
functions.description: Iterate over potential AVOptions-enabled child classes of the given parent class. Returns the next AVClass or NULL when done.
requirements: parent must be a valid AVClass that implements child_class_iterate.
*iter must be an iteration state pointer; pass NULL-initialized to start and reuse between calls.

functions.name: av_opt_find
functions.signature: const AVOption *av_opt_find(void *obj, const char *name, const char *unit, int opt_flags, int search_flags);
functions.description: Find an AVOption by name (and optionally unit), searching obj and optionally its children based on flags. Returns NULL if not found.
requirements: obj must be a pointer to a struct whose first element is AVClass*, or a double pointer to AVClass if AV_OPT_SEARCH_FAKE_OBJ is set in search_flags.
name is the option name to find; unit limits named-constant searches.
opt_flags filters to options having all specified AV_OPT_FLAG_* bits set.
search_flags is a combination of AV_OPT_SEARCH_*; options found via AV_OPT_SEARCH_CHILDREN may not be set directly via av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_find2
functions.signature: const AVOption *av_opt_find2(void *obj, const char *name, const char *unit, int opt_flags, int search_flags, void **target_obj);
functions.description: Like av_opt_find(), but also returns the object that actually owns the found option in target_obj when searching children.
requirements: obj as in av_opt_find().
target_obj, if non-NULL, receives the owning object unless AV_OPT_SEARCH_FAKE_OBJ is set.
name/unit/opt_flags/search_flags semantics same as av_opt_find().

functions.name: av_opt_show2
functions.signature: int av_opt_show2(void *obj, void *av_log_obj, int req_flags, int rej_flags);
functions.description: Log the options of obj via av_log, filtering by requested and rejected flags.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
av_log_obj should be a valid log context (e.g., obj) to control logging.
Only options where (opt->flags & req_flags) and !(opt->flags & rej_flags) are shown.

functions.name: av_opt_get_key_value
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_key_value(const char **ropts, const char *key_val_sep, const char *pairs_sep, unsigned flags, char **rkey, char **rval);
functions.description: Parse a single key-value pair from the beginning of an option string, updating ropts to point past the parsed pair. Allocates rkey and rval on success.
requirements: ropts must point to a NUL-terminated options string; on success it is advanced to the next pair separator or final NUL.
key_val_sep is a 0-terminated list of characters separating key and value.
pairs_sep is a 0-terminated list of characters separating pairs.
flags may include AV_OPT_FLAG_IMPLICIT_KEY to accept values without a key (rkey becomes NULL).
rkey and rval must be freed by the caller using av_free() on success.
Returns AVERROR(EINVAL) if no key is present (and implicit key not allowed).

functions.name: av_set_options_string
functions.signature: int av_set_options_string(void *ctx, const char *opts, const char *key_val_sep, const char *pairs_sep);
functions.description: Parse an options string and set matching fields by name on ctx using AVOptions.
requirements: ctx must be an AVClass context (AVOptions-enabled).
opts may be NULL; otherwise must use provided separators.
key_val_sep and pairs_sep must be character sets distinct from option-name characters and each other.
Returns number of successfully set pairs, or a negative AVERROR: AVERROR(EINVAL) if parsing fails; or error from av_opt_set() for a pair.

functions.name: av_opt_set_from_string
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_from_string(void *ctx, const char *opts, const char *const *shorthand, const char *key_val_sep, const char *pairs_sep);
functions.description: Parse key=value pairs from opts and set corresponding options on ctx, supporting shorthand names when the first fields lack keys.
requirements: ctx must be an AVClass object.
opts is the input string; key/value separated by key_val_sep; pairs separated by pairs_sep.
shorthand is a NULL-terminated array of option names; used for unnamed leading fields until exhausted or a named option is encountered.
Option names must use only characters: a-z A-Z 0-9 - . / _.
Separators must be distinct from each other and from option name characters.
Returns count of successfully set pairs, or AVERROR(EINVAL) if opts cannot be parsed, or error from av_set_string3() if a pair cannot be set.

functions.name: av_opt_set_dict
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_dict(void *obj, struct AVDictionary **options);
functions.description: Apply all options from an AVDictionary to an object. On return, options is replaced with a new dict containing entries not found in obj.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
*options may be NULL or point to a dict; the function frees and replaces it with a dict of unused options; caller must free the new dict with av_dict_free().
Returns 0 on success, negative AVERROR if some found option could not be set.

functions.name: av_opt_set_dict2
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_dict2(void *obj, struct AVDictionary **options, int search_flags);
functions.description: Like av_opt_set_dict(), but allows specifying AV_OPT_SEARCH_* flags for how to search options (e.g., search children).
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
*options ownership and replacement semantics identical to av_opt_set_dict(); caller must free resulting dict.
search_flags is a combination of AV_OPT_SEARCH_*.
Returns 0 on success or negative AVERROR if a found option could not be set.

functions.name: av_opt_copy
functions.signature: int av_opt_copy(void *dest, const void *src);
functions.description: Copy AVOptions values from src to dest. String/binary/dict options are duplicated for dest; original memory is freed unless both point to the same memory. On error, src and dest options will no longer alias.
requirements: dest and src must be AVOptions-enabled objects with the same underlying AVClass; otherwise guarantees do not apply.
Caller must manage lifetime of dest and src; this copies option values only.
Returns 0 on success, negative on error.

functions.name: av_opt_set
functions.signature: int av_opt_set(void *obj, const char *name, const char *val, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set an option by name using a string value. Non-string types are parsed from the string according to the option type. Supports numeric scalars with SI postfixes, named scalars, and flags sequences with '+'/'-' combining.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must match an existing option; otherwise returns AVERROR_OPTION_NOT_FOUND.

val format must match the option type: numeric or named scalar for numeric; '+'/'-' separated flags for flags; for dict type, ':'-separated key=value pairs with escaping for ':'; for strings/binary, appropriate string or escaped data.
search_flags is passed to av_opt_find2 and may include AV_OPT_SEARCH_CHILDREN.
Returns 0 on success; AVERROR_OPTION_NOT_FOUND if no match; AVERROR(ERANGE) if out of range; AVERROR(EINVAL) if invalid value.

functions.name: av_opt_set_int
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_int(void *obj, const char *name, int64_t val, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set an integer-compatible option by name from an int64_t value.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an integer-compatible option; otherwise AVERROR(EINVAL) or AVERROR_OPTION_NOT_FOUND.
Value must be within the option’s allowed range or AVERROR(ERANGE) is returned.
search_flags as in av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_set_double
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_double(void *obj, const char *name, double val, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set a floating-point-compatible option by name from a double value.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference a double/float-compatible option.
Value must be within the allowed range or AVERROR(ERANGE).
search_flags as in av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_set_q
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_q(void *obj, const char *name, AVRational val, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set an AVRational-compatible option by name.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference a rational-compatible option.
search_flags as in av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_set_bin
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_bin(void *obj, const char *name, const uint8_t *val, int size, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set a binary option from a byte array of length size.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference a binary-compatible option.
val may be NULL with size 0 to clear; behavior otherwise must match the option type.
search_flags as in av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_set_image_size
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_image_size(void *obj, const char *name, int w, int h, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set an image size option (two consecutive integers), providing width and height.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_IMAGE_SIZE option.
w and h must be within allowed ranges.
search_flags as in av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_set_pixel_fmt
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_pixel_fmt(void *obj, const char *name, enum AVPixelFormat fmt, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set a pixel format option from an AVPixelFormat value.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_PIXEL_FMT option.
search_flags as in av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_set_sample_fmt
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_sample_fmt(void *obj, const char *name, enum AVSampleFormat fmt, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set a sample format option from an AVSampleFormat value.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_SAMPLE_FMT option.
search_flags as in av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_set_video_rate
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_video_rate(void *obj, const char *name, AVRational val, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set a video rate (frame rate) option from an AVRational value.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_VIDEO_RATE option.
search_flags as in av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_set_chlayout
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_chlayout(void *obj, const char *name, const AVChannelLayout *layout, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set a channel layout option from an AVChannelLayout. Any old layout present is discarded and replaced with a copy.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_CHLAYOUT option.
Caller retains ownership of layout and must uninitialize it when appropriate.
search_flags as in av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_set_dict_val
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_dict_val(void *obj, const char *name, const AVDictionary *val, int search_flags);
functions.description: Set a dictionary option from an AVDictionary. Any old dictionary present is discarded and replaced with a copy.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_DICT option.
Caller retains ownership of val and is responsible for freeing it.
search_flags as in av_opt_set().

functions.name: av_opt_set_array
functions.signature: int av_opt_set_array(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, unsigned int start_elem, unsigned int nb_elems, enum AVOptionType val_type, const void *val);
functions.description: Modify elements of an array-type option: insert/replace elements from val or remove elements when val is NULL. Behavior may be altered with AV_OPT_ARRAY_REPLACE in search_flags.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled and name must reference an array option (AV_OPT_TYPE_FLAG_ARRAY combined with a base type).
start_elem must not be larger than current array size (from av_opt_get_array_size()).
If val is NULL, start_elem+nb_elems must not exceed array size (elements are removed and remaining elements shifted).
If val is non-NULL, val must point to an array with nb_elems elements whose C type matches val_type.
val_type specifies which av_opt_setX() semantics apply per element (e.g., AV_OPT_TYPE_STRING corresponds to av_opt_set()).
If AV_OPT_ARRAY_REPLACE is set, elements in [start_elem, start_elem+nb_elems) are replaced; otherwise elements are inserted and later elements shifted.

functions.name: av_opt_get
functions.signature: int av_opt_get(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, uint8_t **out_val);
functions.description: Get an option’s value as a string (allocated). For pointer types set to NULL, returns NULL if AV_OPT_ALLOW_NULL is set in search_flags; otherwise returns an allocated empty string.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an existing option; search_flags controls child search and AV_OPT_ALLOW_NULL behavior.
On success, *out_val is av_malloc()'d and must be freed with av_free() unless NULL was returned due to AV_OPT_ALLOW_NULL.

functions.name: av_opt_get_int
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_int(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, int64_t *out_val);
functions.description: Get an integer-compatible option value as int64_t.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an integer-compatible option; search_flags as in av_opt_get().
out_val must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_get_double
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_double(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, double *out_val);
functions.description: Get a floating-point-compatible option value as double.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference a float/double-compatible option; search_flags as in av_opt_get().
out_val must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_get_q
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_q(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, AVRational *out_val);
functions.description: Get a rational-compatible option value as AVRational.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference a rational-compatible option; search_flags as in av_opt_get().
out_val must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_get_image_size
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_image_size(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, int *w_out, int *h_out);
functions.description: Get an image size option, returning width and height through w_out and h_out.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_IMAGE_SIZE option; search_flags as in av_opt_get().
w_out and h_out must be valid pointers.

functions.name: av_opt_get_pixel_fmt
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_pixel_fmt(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, enum AVPixelFormat *out_fmt);
functions.description: Get a pixel format option value.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_PIXEL_FMT option; search_flags as in av_opt_get().
out_fmt must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_get_sample_fmt
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_sample_fmt(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, enum AVSampleFormat *out_fmt);
functions.description: Get a sample format option value.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_SAMPLE_FMT option; search_flags as in av_opt_get().
out_fmt must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_get_video_rate
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_video_rate(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, AVRational *out_val);
functions.description: Get a video rate (frame rate) option value.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_VIDEO_RATE option; search_flags as in av_opt_get().
out_val must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_get_chlayout
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_chlayout(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, AVChannelLayout *layout);
functions.description: Get a channel layout option value. Returns a copy in layout; caller must free with av_channel_layout_uninit().
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_CHLAYOUT option; search_flags as in av_opt_get().
layout must be a valid pointer to receive a copy and must be uninitialized by the caller before passing; caller must call av_channel_layout_uninit() on it.

functions.name: av_opt_get_dict_val
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_dict_val(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, AVDictionary **out_val);
functions.description: Get a dictionary option value. Returns a copy via out_val; caller must free with av_dict_free().
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an AV_OPT_TYPE_DICT option; search_flags as in av_opt_get().
out_val must be a valid pointer; on success, *out_val must be freed with av_dict_free().

functions.name: av_opt_get_array_size
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_array_size(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, unsigned int *out_val);
functions.description: For an array-type option, get the number of elements present.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must reference an array-type option.
out_val must be a valid pointer.
search_flags as in av_opt_get().

functions.name: av_opt_get_array
functions.signature: int av_opt_get_array(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags, unsigned int start_elem, unsigned int nb_elems, enum AVOptionType out_type, void *out_val);
functions.description: Retrieve one or more array elements from an array-type option and convert each element to the requested out_type, writing results into out_val array.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled; name must reference an array-type option.
start_elem and nb_elems must define a range within the current array size (as from av_opt_get_array_size()).
out_type specifies which av_opt_getX() semantics to apply per element (e.g., AV_OPT_TYPE_STRING corresponds to av_opt_get()).
out_val must point to an array with nb_elems members, zeroed on entry, and its C type must match out_type.
For dynamically allocated outputs (strings, binary, dicts), caller owns and must free results.

functions.name: av_opt_eval_flags
functions.signature: int av_opt_eval_flags(void *obj, const AVOption *o, const char *val, int *flags_out);
functions.description: Parse val according to the flags-type option o and write the resulting flags into flags_out.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
o must be a valid AVOption of flags type belonging to obj.
val must be a string acceptable for flags parsing (numeric/named flags with '+'/'-' as documented for av_opt_set()).
flags_out must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_eval_int
functions.signature: int av_opt_eval_int(void *obj, const AVOption *o, const char *val, int *int_out);
functions.description: Parse val as an integer according to option o and write into int_out.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
o must be an integer-compatible AVOption belonging to obj.
val must be parseable per option semantics (supports scalars/named).
int_out must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_eval_uint
functions.signature: int av_opt_eval_uint(void *obj, const AVOption *o, const char *val, unsigned *uint_out);
functions.description: Parse val as an unsigned integer according to option o and write into uint_out.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
o must be an unsigned-int-compatible AVOption belonging to obj.
val must be parseable per option semantics.
uint_out must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_eval_int64
functions.signature: int av_opt_eval_int64(void *obj, const AVOption *o, const char *val, int64_t *int64_out);
functions.description: Parse val as a 64-bit integer according to option o and write into int64_out.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
o must be an int64-compatible AVOption belonging to obj.
val must be parseable per option semantics.
int64_out must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_eval_float
functions.signature: int av_opt_eval_float(void *obj, const AVOption *o, const char *val, float *float_out);
functions.description: Parse val as a float according to option o and write into float_out.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
o must be a float-compatible AVOption belonging to obj.
val must be parseable per option semantics.
float_out must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_eval_double
functions.signature: int av_opt_eval_double(void *obj, const AVOption *o, const char *val, double *double_out);
functions.description: Parse val as a double according to option o and write into double_out.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
o must be a double-compatible AVOption belonging to obj.
val must be parseable per option semantics.
double_out must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_eval_q
functions.signature: int av_opt_eval_q(void *obj, const AVOption *o, const char *val, AVRational *q_out);
functions.description: Parse val as an AVRational according to option o and write into q_out.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
o must be a rational-compatible AVOption belonging to obj.
val must be parseable per option semantics.
q_out must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: av_opt_is_set_to_default
functions.signature: int av_opt_is_set_to_default(void *obj, const AVOption *o);
functions.description: Check if the given option on obj is set to its default value.
requirements: obj must be an AVClass object containing option o (do not use for child options).
o must belong to obj’s AVOptions.
Returns >0 if set to default, 0 if not, <0 on error.

functions.name: av_opt_is_set_to_default_by_name
functions.signature: int av_opt_is_set_to_default_by_name(void *obj, const char *name, int search_flags);
functions.description: Check if the named option on obj (or its children per search_flags) is set to its default value.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
name must exist; search_flags controls where to search.
Returns >0 if set to default, 0 if not, <0 on error.

functions.name: av_opt_flag_is_set
functions.signature: int av_opt_flag_is_set(void *obj, const char *field_name, const char *flag_name);
functions.description: Test whether a specific flag is set in a flags-type option field.
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
field_name must name a flags field option; flag_name must be a valid named flag within that option’s unit.
Returns non-zero if set; zero if not set, wrong type, or field not found.

functions.name: av_opt_serialize
functions.signature: int av_opt_serialize(void *obj, int opt_flags, int flags, char **buffer, const char key_val_sep, const char pairs_sep);
functions.description: Serialize an object’s options into a newly allocated string suitable for round-tripping with av_opt_set_from_string(). Escapes separators via av_escape().
requirements: obj must be AVOptions-enabled.
opt_flags filters to options with all specified AV_OPT_FLAG_* bits set.
flags is a combination of AV_OPT_SERIALIZE_* (e.g., SKIP_DEFAULTS, OPT_FLAGS_EXACT, SEARCH_CHILDREN).
buffer receives an av_malloc()'d string that the caller must free when no longer needed.
key_val_sep and pairs_sep cannot be '\\' nor '\0' and cannot be the same character.

functions.name: av_opt_freep_ranges
functions.signature: void av_opt_freep_ranges(AVOptionRanges **ranges);
functions.description: Free an AVOptionRanges list and set the pointer to NULL.
requirements: ranges must be a valid pointer to an AVOptionRanges*; safe to call with *ranges == NULL.
Caller must not use the freed ranges afterwards.

functions.name: av_opt_query_ranges
functions.signature: int av_opt_query_ranges(AVOptionRanges **, void *obj, const char *key, int flags);
functions.description: Get the allowed value ranges for a given option key on obj, possibly depending on other fields. Returns number of components on success. Result must be freed with av_opt_freep_ranges().
requirements: First argument must be a pointer to AVOptionRanges* receiving the result; caller must later free it with av_opt_freep_ranges().
obj must be AVOptions-enabled, or a double pointer to AVClass if AV_OPT_SEARCH_FAKE_OBJ is set in flags.
key is the option name whose ranges are requested.
flags is a bitmask; may include AV_OPT_SEARCH_FAKE_OBJ and AV_OPT_MULTI_COMPONENT_RANGE.
Returns negative error code on failure.

functions.name: av_opt_query_ranges_default
functions.signature: int av_opt_query_ranges_default(AVOptionRanges **, void *obj, const char *key, int flags);
functions.description: Get the default allowed ranges for the given option key without using AVClass.query_ranges(), useful as a fallback. Returns number of components on success. Result must be freed with av_opt_freep_ranges().
requirements: First argument must be a pointer to AVOptionRanges* receiving the result; caller must later free it with av_opt_freep_ranges().
obj must be AVOptions-enabled, or a double pointer to AVClass if AV_OPT_SEARCH_FAKE_OBJ is set in flags.
key is the option name.
flags may include AV_OPT_SEARCH_FAKE_OBJ and AV_OPT_MULTI_COMPONENT_RANGE.
Returns negative error code on failure.

functions.name: av_make_q
functions.signature: static inline AVRational av_make_q(int num, int den)
functions.description: Constructs an AVRational from the given numerator and denominator without reducing it. Useful where compound literals are not supported. Returns the pair {num, den} exactly as provided.
requirements: num and den are stored as 32-bit signed integers; values outside int range are invalid.
The returned rational is not reduced; callers needing a reduced form must call av_reduce().

functions.name: av_cmp_q
functions.signature: static inline int av_cmp_q(AVRational a, AVRational b)
functions.description: Compares two rationals a and b. Returns 0 if equal, 1 if a > b, -1 if a < b, or INT_MIN if one of the values is 0/0. Handles zero denominators and signs according to the implementation.
requirements: Inputs must be initialized AVRational values.
If either input is 0/0, the return value is INT_MIN and does not represent an ordering.

functions.name: av_q2d
functions.signature: static inline double av_q2d(AVRational a)
functions.description: Converts an AVRational to a double-precision floating-point value by computing a.num / (double)a.den. Equivalent to av_q2d(a).
requirements: Input must be an initialized AVRational.
If a.den == 0, the result will be +/-inf or NaN depending on a.num, per IEEE floating-point division semantics.

functions.name: av_reduce
functions.signature: int av_reduce(int *dst_num, int *dst_den, int64_t num, int64_t den, int64_t max)
functions.description: Reduces the fraction num/den to a simpler ratio not exceeding max in numerator or denominator, writing the result to dst_num and dst_den. Often used for framerate calculations. Returns 1 if the reduction is exact, 0 otherwise.
requirements: dst_num and dst_den must be valid, non-null pointers.
max is the maximum allowed absolute value for both dst_num and dst_den; it should be positive (acts as a bound).
num and den are 64-bit integers; den may be zero to represent special values, in which case behavior follows the library’s reduction rules.
Callers must check the return value to know if the operation was exact (1) or not (0).

functions.name: av_mul_q
functions.signature: AVRational av_mul_q(AVRational b, AVRational c) av_const
functions.description: Returns the product of two rationals, b * c, as an AVRational. Marked av_const (no observable state access).
requirements: Inputs must be initialized AVRational values.
Result may not be reduced; reduce with av_reduce() if needed.

functions.name: av_div_q
functions.signature: AVRational av_div_q(AVRational b, AVRational c) av_const
functions.description: Returns the quotient of two rationals, b / c, as an AVRational. Marked av_const (no observable state access).
requirements: Inputs must be initialized AVRational values.
Division by a zero rational (c.num == 0 and c.den != 0) or 0/0 may yield infinities/undefined rationals; callers should validate inputs if such cases are not desired.
Result may not be reduced; reduce with av_reduce() if needed.

functions.name: av_add_q
functions.signature: AVRational av_add_q(AVRational b, AVRational c) av_const
functions.description: Returns the sum of two rationals, b + c, as an AVRational. Marked av_const (no observable state access).
requirements: Inputs must be initialized AVRational values.
Result may not be reduced; reduce with av_reduce() if needed.

functions.name: av_sub_q
functions.signature: AVRational av_sub_q(AVRational b, AVRational c) av_const
functions.description: Returns the difference of two rationals, b - c, as an AVRational. Marked av_const (no observable state access).
requirements: Inputs must be initialized AVRational values.
Result may not be reduced; reduce with av_reduce() if needed.

functions.name: av_inv_q
functions.signature: static av_always_inline AVRational av_inv_q(AVRational q)
functions.description: Returns the multiplicative inverse of q, i.e., {q.den, q.num}. Simple swap of numerator and denominator.
requirements: Input must be an initialized AVRational.
If q.num == 0, the result has denominator 0, representing an infinite or undefined value by convention.

functions.name: av_d2q
functions.signature: AVRational av_d2q(double d, int max) av_const
functions.description: Converts a double to the closest representable AVRational with numerator and denominator limited by max. Returns {1,0} or {-1,0} for +/-infinity. Many rationals with |num|,|den| <= 1<<26 can be recovered exactly from double.
requirements: max is the maximum allowed absolute value for numerator and denominator and should be positive.
Input d may be finite, +/-infinity, or NaN; infinities map to {±1,0}. Behavior for NaN is not documented and should be handled by the caller as needed.

functions.name: av_nearer_q
functions.signature: int av_nearer_q(AVRational q, AVRational q1, AVRational q2)
functions.description: Compares distances of q1 and q2 to q and returns 1 if q1 is nearer, -1 if q2 is nearer, or 0 if they are equally near.
requirements: Inputs must be initialized AVRational values.

functions.name: av_find_nearest_q_idx
functions.signature: int av_find_nearest_q_idx(AVRational q, const AVRational* q_list)
functions.description: Given a reference rational q and a list of rationals terminated by {0,0}, returns the index of the list element nearest to q.
requirements: q_list must be a valid, non-null pointer to an array of AVRational elements terminated by a sentinel {0,0}.
The array must be accessible up to and including the sentinel.

functions.name: av_q2intfloat
functions.signature: uint32_t av_q2intfloat(AVRational q)
functions.description: Converts an AVRational to an IEEE 754 single-precision float value encoded in a platform-independent 32-bit unsigned integer representation (fixed conversion).
requirements: Input must be an initialized AVRational.

functions.name: av_gcd_q
functions.signature: AVRational av_gcd_q(AVRational a, AVRational b, int max_den, AVRational def)
functions.description: Returns the greatest common rational such that both a and b are integer multiples of it. If the resulting denominator would exceed max_den, returns def instead.
requirements: Inputs must be initialized AVRational values.
max_den is a positive bound on the denominator of the result.
def is the default AVRational to return when the computed denominator would be larger than max_den.

functions.name: av_get_bits_per_pixel
functions.signature: int av_get_bits_per_pixel(const AVPixFmtDescriptor *pixdesc);
functions.description: Returns the number of bits actually used to store one pixel for the given pixel format descriptor (padding bits are not counted). Use to compute storage needs or iterate component packing.
requirements: pixdesc must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an AVPixFmtDescriptor (e.g., obtained from av_pix_fmt_desc_get or av_pix_fmt_desc_next).
Caller must handle any format-specific packing as this returns bits used, not bits per sample.

functions.name: av_get_padded_bits_per_pixel
functions.signature: int av_get_padded_bits_per_pixel(const AVPixFmtDescriptor *pixdesc);
functions.description: Returns the number of bits per pixel including any padding/unused bits for the pixel format described by pixdesc.
requirements: pixdesc must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an AVPixFmtDescriptor.

functions.name: av_pix_fmt_desc_get
functions.signature: const AVPixFmtDescriptor *av_pix_fmt_desc_get(enum AVPixelFormat pix_fmt);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the pixel format descriptor for pix_fmt, or NULL if the format is unknown.
requirements: pix_fmt may be any AVPixelFormat; caller must check for NULL before dereferencing the returned pointer.

functions.name: av_pix_fmt_desc_next
functions.signature: const AVPixFmtDescriptor *av_pix_fmt_desc_next(const AVPixFmtDescriptor *prev);
functions.description: Iterates over all pixel format descriptors known to libavutil. Pass NULL to get the first descriptor, then pass the previous return value to get the next until NULL is returned.
requirements: If prev is non-NULL, it should be a pointer previously returned by this function (do not pass arbitrary pointers).
Iteration must stop when NULL is returned.

functions.name: av_pix_fmt_desc_get_id
functions.signature: enum AVPixelFormat av_pix_fmt_desc_get_id(const AVPixFmtDescriptor *desc);
functions.description: Returns the AVPixelFormat corresponding to desc, or AV_PIX_FMT_NONE if desc is not a valid pointer to a pixel format descriptor.
requirements: desc should be a valid descriptor pointer (e.g., returned by av_pix_fmt_desc_get or av_pix_fmt_desc_next).
Caller must handle AV_PIX_FMT_NONE as an invalid/unknown descriptor indicator.

functions.name: av_pix_fmt_get_chroma_sub_sample
functions.signature: int av_pix_fmt_get_chroma_sub_sample(enum AVPixelFormat pix_fmt, int *h_shift, int *v_shift);
functions.description: Retrieves log2 chroma subsampling factors from the pixel format descriptor. Writes log2_chroma_w to h_shift and log2_chroma_h to v_shift.
requirements: h_shift must be a non-NULL pointer to int for output.
v_shift must be a non-NULL pointer to int for output.
Returns 0 on success; returns a negative AVERROR (AVERROR(ENOSYS)) if pix_fmt is invalid or unknown; caller must check return value.
pix_fmt should be a valid AVPixelFormat; for formats without chroma subsampling values may be 0.

functions.name: av_pix_fmt_count_planes
functions.signature: int av_pix_fmt_count_planes(enum AVPixelFormat pix_fmt);
functions.description: Returns the number of planes for the pixel format, or a negative AVERROR if pix_fmt is not a valid pixel format.
requirements: Caller must check for negative return values indicating errors.
pix_fmt should be a valid AVPixelFormat.

functions.name: av_color_range_name
functions.signature: const char *av_color_range_name(enum AVColorRange range);
functions.description: Returns the short name string for the given color range, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: range may be any AVColorRange; caller must check for NULL return before use.

functions.name: av_color_range_from_name
functions.signature: int av_color_range_from_name(const char *name);
functions.description: Parses a color range name and returns the corresponding AVColorRange value, or an AVError if not found.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
Caller must check for negative return values (AVError) indicating the name was not found.

functions.name: av_color_primaries_name
functions.signature: const char *av_color_primaries_name(enum AVColorPrimaries primaries);
functions.description: Returns the short name string for the given color primaries, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: primaries may be any AVColorPrimaries; caller must check for NULL return.

functions.name: av_color_primaries_from_name
functions.signature: int av_color_primaries_from_name(const char *name);
functions.description: Parses a color primaries name and returns the corresponding AVColorPrimaries value, or an AVError if not found.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
Caller must check for negative return values (AVError).

functions.name: av_color_transfer_name
functions.signature: const char *av_color_transfer_name(enum AVColorTransferCharacteristic transfer);
functions.description: Returns the short name string for the given color transfer characteristic, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: transfer may be any AVColorTransferCharacteristic; caller must check for NULL return.

functions.name: av_color_transfer_from_name
functions.signature: int av_color_transfer_from_name(const char *name);
functions.description: Parses a color transfer name and returns the corresponding AVColorTransferCharacteristic value, or an AVError if not found.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
Caller must check for negative return values (AVError).

functions.name: av_color_space_name
functions.signature: const char *av_color_space_name(enum AVColorSpace space);
functions.description: Returns the short name string for the given color space, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: space may be any AVColorSpace; caller must check for NULL return.

functions.name: av_color_space_from_name
functions.signature: int av_color_space_from_name(const char *name);
functions.description: Parses a color space name and returns the corresponding AVColorSpace value, or an AVError if not found.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
Caller must check for negative return values (AVError).

functions.name: av_chroma_location_name
functions.signature: const char *av_chroma_location_name(enum AVChromaLocation location);
functions.description: Returns the short name string for the given chroma location, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: location may be any AVChromaLocation; caller must check for NULL return.

functions.name: av_chroma_location_from_name
functions.signature: int av_chroma_location_from_name(const char *name);
functions.description: Parses a chroma location name and returns the corresponding AVChromaLocation value, or an AVError if not found.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
Caller must check for negative return values (AVError).

functions.name: av_chroma_location_enum_to_pos
functions.signature: int av_chroma_location_enum_to_pos(int *xpos, int *ypos, enum AVChromaLocation pos);
functions.description: Converts an AVChromaLocation enum to swscale-style x/y chroma sample positions. Positions report the chroma (0,0) location in a system where luma (0,0) is origin and luma(1,1) is 256,256.
requirements: xpos must be a non-NULL pointer to int for output.
ypos must be a non-NULL pointer to int for output.
pos should be a valid AVChromaLocation.
Caller must check the integer return value for success/failure (nonzero indicates failure per typical AVERROR usage; exact error codes not documented here).

functions.name: av_chroma_location_pos_to_enum
functions.signature: enum AVChromaLocation av_chroma_location_pos_to_enum(int xpos, int ypos);
functions.description: Converts swscale-style x/y chroma sample positions to the closest AVChromaLocation enum. The positions represent chroma (0,0) with luma(1,1)=256,256.
requirements: xpos and ypos should be in the 0..256 coordinate scale used by swscale chroma positioning (inferred from documentation).
Caller must handle that the return may be an enum representing the best match; behavior for out-of-range inputs is unspecified.

functions.name: av_alpha_mode_name
functions.signature: const char *av_alpha_mode_name(enum AVAlphaMode mode);
functions.description: Returns the name for the provided alpha mode, or NULL if unknown.
requirements: mode may be any AVAlphaMode; caller must check for NULL return.

functions.name: av_alpha_mode_from_name
functions.signature: enum AVAlphaMode av_alpha_mode_from_name(const char *name);
functions.description: Parses an alpha mode name and returns the corresponding AVAlphaMode value, or an AVError if not found.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
Caller must be prepared for error returns (library uses AVError codes when not found).

functions.name: av_get_pix_fmt
functions.signature: enum AVPixelFormat av_get_pix_fmt(const char *name);
functions.description: Returns the AVPixelFormat corresponding to the given name. If not found, tries the native-endian variant (e.g., gray16 -> gray16le on little-endian). Returns AV_PIX_FMT_NONE if no format matches.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
Caller must handle AV_PIX_FMT_NONE if the name is not recognized.

functions.name: av_get_pix_fmt_name
functions.signature: const char *av_get_pix_fmt_name(enum AVPixelFormat pix_fmt);
functions.description: Returns the short name for a pixel format, or NULL if pix_fmt is unknown.
requirements: pix_fmt may be any AVPixelFormat; caller must check for NULL return.

functions.name: av_get_pix_fmt_string
functions.signature: char *av_get_pix_fmt_string(char *buf, int buf_size, enum AVPixelFormat pix_fmt);
functions.description: Writes a human-readable string for the pixel format number pix_fmt into buf, or a header if pix_fmt is negative. Returns buf.
requirements: buf must be a valid, writable buffer pointer.
buf_size must be the size of buf in bytes and >= 1.
If pix_fmt is negative, function writes a header string; otherwise writes info for the specified pixel format.
Caller must ensure buf is large enough for the output to avoid truncation.

functions.name: av_read_image_line2
functions.signature: void av_read_image_line2(void *dst, const uint8_t *data[4], const int linesize[4], const AVPixFmtDescriptor *desc, int x, int y, int c, int w, int read_pal_component, int dst_element_size);
functions.description: Reads a horizontal line of component values from an image and writes component c values to dst according to the pixel format descriptor. Supports paletted formats if read_pal_component is nonzero. Element size in dst must be 2 or 4 bytes.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer large enough for w elements of size dst_element_size bytes.
data must be an array of up to 4 valid plane pointers for the image being read.
linesize must contain valid line strides (in bytes or bits per format) for each corresponding data plane.
desc must be a valid descriptor describing the pixel format of the image.
x and y must reference pixels within the actual image bounds (out-of-bounds behavior is undefined).
c must be a valid component index for the format (0..3; alpha is last if present).
w must be the number of component values to read; must be >= 0.
If read_pal_component is nonzero, the format must be paletted; behavior is undefined otherwise.
dst_element_size must be 2 or 4 (per documentation).
For bitstream formats, elements may be in bits; caller must provide consistent buffers and parameters.

functions.name: av_read_image_line
functions.signature: void av_read_image_line(uint16_t *dst, const uint8_t *data[4], const int linesize[4], const AVPixFmtDescriptor *desc, int x, int y, int c, int w, int read_pal_component);
functions.description: Reads a horizontal line of component values from an image and writes component c values to dst (16-bit elements). Supports paletted formats if read_pal_component is nonzero.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer large enough for w uint16_t elements.
data must be an array of up to 4 valid plane pointers for the image.
linesize must contain valid line strides for each data plane.
desc must be a valid descriptor matching the image format.
x and y must be within image bounds; c must be a valid component index (0..3).
w must be >= 0.
If read_pal_component is nonzero, the format must be paletted; behavior is undefined otherwise.

functions.name: av_write_image_line2
functions.signature: void av_write_image_line2(const void *src, uint8_t *data[4], const int linesize[4], const AVPixFmtDescriptor *desc, int x, int y, int c, int w, int src_element_size);
functions.description: Writes w component c values from src into the image line at (x,y) according to the pixel format descriptor. Element size in src must be 2 or 4 bytes. Intended for images whose planes array is zeroed before writing.
requirements: src must point to a readable buffer containing at least w elements of size src_element_size bytes.
data must be an array of up to 4 valid plane pointers for the destination image and is supposed to be zeroed before writing (per documentation).
linesize must contain valid line strides for each plane.
desc must be a valid descriptor matching the destination image format.
x and y must reference pixels within the image bounds; c must be a valid component index for the format (0..3).
w must be >= 0.
src_element_size must be 2 or 4 (per documentation).

functions.name: av_write_image_line
functions.signature: void av_write_image_line(const uint16_t *src, uint8_t *data[4], const int linesize[4], const AVPixFmtDescriptor *desc, int x, int y, int c, int w);
functions.description: Writes w 16-bit component c values from src into the image line at (x,y) according to the pixel format descriptor. The destination planes array is supposed to be zeroed before writing.
requirements: src must point to a readable buffer containing at least w uint16_t elements.
data must be an array of up to 4 valid plane pointers for the destination image and is supposed to be zeroed before writing.
linesize must contain valid line strides for each plane.
desc must be a valid descriptor for the destination image format.
x and y must be within image bounds; c must be a valid component index (0..3).
w must be >= 0.

functions.name: av_pix_fmt_swap_endianness
functions.signature: enum AVPixelFormat av_pix_fmt_swap_endianness(enum AVPixelFormat pix_fmt);
functions.description: Returns the pixel format with swapped endianness if a counterpart exists; otherwise returns AV_PIX_FMT_NONE.
requirements: pix_fmt should be an endianness-specific format to have a swappable counterpart; caller must handle AV_PIX_FMT_NONE if no counterpart exists.

functions.name: av_get_pix_fmt_loss
functions.signature: int av_get_pix_fmt_loss(enum AVPixelFormat dst_pix_fmt, enum AVPixelFormat src_pix_fmt, int has_alpha);
functions.description: Computes and returns a combination of FF_LOSS_* flags describing information loss when converting from src_pix_fmt to dst_pix_fmt (e.g., chroma, resolution, depth, colorspace, alpha, quantization). If dst_pix_fmt is invalid, returns maximum loss.
requirements: dst_pix_fmt and src_pix_fmt may be any AVPixelFormat; caller must interpret the returned bitmask.
has_alpha indicates whether the source alpha channel is used and must be set appropriately for accurate loss reporting.

functions.name: av_find_best_pix_fmt_of_2
functions.signature: enum AVPixelFormat av_find_best_pix_fmt_of_2(enum AVPixelFormat dst_pix_fmt1, enum AVPixelFormat dst_pix_fmt2, enum AVPixelFormat src_pix_fmt, int has_alpha, int *loss_ptr);
functions.description: Chooses the better of two destination pixel formats for converting from src_pix_fmt, minimizing information loss. Returns the selected destination format. If loss_ptr is provided, it receives the loss flags for the chosen format.
requirements: dst_pix_fmt1 and dst_pix_fmt2 are candidate destination formats; at least one should be a valid AVPixelFormat.
src_pix_fmt is the source format; should be valid for meaningful results.
